part1.desc: Verifies that no commons modules (see import-rules check) are nested in other commons modules.
part1.rationale: Make reasoning about commons modules easier

exception.desc: `c` modules may be nested inside`c` modules (e.g. `/c/foo/c/bar`). There may be as much nesting of these as desired.
exception.rationale: It's commonly necessary to nest `c` commons modules to share code within a `c` module.

part2.desc: For `t`, `s`, `cnst`, and `ext_traits` commons modules, verifies that every module declaration in all mod.rs file is: - private (i.e. `mod x;`, never `pub mod x;`); and - glob re-exported (i.e. `pub use x::*;`).
part2.rationale: So that users can import `use ...::t::TypeName` (i.e. not `use ...::t::submodule::TypeName`), saving characters.
part2.exception: The glob re-export is not required when the module exposes no public items to re-export (e.g. a module containing only `impl` blocks).

part3.desc: Verifies that all `mod.rs` files in a `c` commons module: - Declares all of its modules as public (i.e. `pub mod ...`); and - Contains no `use` statements.
part3.rationale: So callers of the `c` module can import the submodules and call the functions (e.g. submodule::fn_name())
part3.exception: If the module contains a nested `c` module, the `mod.rs` must instead: - Declare the nested module privately as `mod c;` (annotated with the outer attribute `#[allow(clippy::module_inception)]` if needed); and - Have a single `pub use c::*;` glob statement re-exporting the nested `c` module.
